title: Nifty sinks below 22,400, breadth collapses as metal, finance stocks lead rout - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Only four Nifty 50 constituents were in the green. Eternal led gainers with a rise of 2.38 per cent to ₹311.70 from ₹304.45. TCS held on to a 0.84 per cent gain at ₹2,528 from ₹2,506.90, while Infosys edged up 0.13 per cent to ₹1,154.90 from ₹1,153.35, and ONGC barely gained 0.04 per cent to ₹225.09 from ₹225.00. IT remained the only Nifty sectoral index in positive territory for the session. | Photo Credit: istock.com

Markets came under severe selling pressure by midday on Friday, with early gains evaporating rapidly as broad-based declines swept across sectors. The Sensex, which had opened at 73,665.64 against a previous close of 73,249.39, was trading at 72,523.94, down 725.45 points or 0.99 per cent, at 12:50 pm. The Nifty 50, which opened at 22,742.20 against a previous close of 22,687.65, had fallen to 22,393.80, down 293.85 points or 1.30 per cent.

Market breadth on BSE painted a stark picture. Of 4,379 stocks traded, 3,598 declined against just 580 advances, with 201 unchanged. As many as 645 stocks hit 52-week lows, compared to just 52 at 52-week highs. The Nifty Midcap 100 tumbled 2.9 per cent while the Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 3.5 per cent, marking the fourth consecutive session in which frontline indices posted a lower intraday low. The Nifty’s advance-decline ratio stood at a deeply skewed 4:46.

“Frontline indices posted a lower intraday low compared to their previous session for the fourth consecutive trading session. Intensive selling pressure is being witnessed in the broader market,” SBI Securities said in its mid-market update.

HDFC Bank shares hover 52-week low ahead of CEO handover on Monday

Metals were the worst-hit sector. Tata Steel led Nifty 50 losses, plunging 4.97 per cent to ₹163.76 from a previous close of ₹172.33. TMPV fell 3.65 per cent to ₹260.15 from ₹270.00, and Adani Ports dropped 3.30 per cent to ₹1,692.20 from ₹1,750.00. In the financial space, Jio Financial Services slid 3.55 per cent to ₹203.31 from ₹210.80, while Shriram Finance — which is scheduled to declare quarterly results today — fell 3.38 per cent to ₹870.45 from ₹900.90. Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, Infosys and JSW Steel are also on the results calendar for the day.

Only four Nifty 50 constituents were in the green. Eternal led gainers with a rise of 2.38 per cent to ₹311.70 from ₹304.45. TCS held on to a 0.84 per cent gain at ₹2,528 from ₹2,506.90, while Infosys edged up 0.13 per cent to ₹1,154.90 from ₹1,153.35, and ONGC barely gained 0.04 per cent to ₹225.09 from ₹225.00. IT remained the only Nifty sectoral index in positive territory for the session.

Crude oil prices continued to drive uncertainty. WTI crude crossed $100 per barrel, trading around $100.10, up 1 per cent, while Brent hovered above $113 after settling at $113.17 the previous day — its highest close since May. MCX crude oil was trading around ₹9,525, up 0.42 per cent.

“Brent near $114 is no longer just creating temporary pressure on sentiment; if sustained, it could keep inflation expectations elevated and gradually affect consumption and corporate profitability,” said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth.

Gold and silver came under pressure. COMEX gold fell 0.82 per cent to around $4,027, an 11-week low, while COMEX silver dropped 1.84 per cent to around $54.00 and was deep in oversold territory with an RSI near 29. Domestically, MCX gold declined 0.60 per cent to around ₹142,450 and MCX silver fell 1.78 per cent to around ₹196,050, with the latter’s RSI near 24, signalling extreme oversold conditions. The rupee was trading around 94.80 to the dollar, having snapped an eight-session winning streak the previous day.

NIFTY IT gives up intraday gains, but sector posts sharp monthly recovery

On the technicals, SBI Securities pegged the critical Nifty support at 22,300–22,320, with a breach potentially opening downside to 22,130–22,150. Sensex support lies at 72,300. Nifty resistance is seen at 22,610–22,630.

“The market can move higher anticipating the liquidity surge from IPO refunds next week, but the rally will be led by large-caps. The sharp correction in small-caps might continue since their valuations, driven up by liquidity rather than fundamentals, are hard to justify,” said Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments.
